cu.auto.lead: Add this service to your Project's compose file, alongside the nzbfast service, and it checks nightly at 04:00 for a newer image. Set the timezone to yours.

cu.intro: nzbfast is running in a container, so it never replaces its own files: you move it forward by pulling a newer image. Your settings, queue and downloads live in the folders you mounted, and survive the swap.
cu.now.click: If you created it by searching the Registry and clicking Run: Registry → re-download the latest tag, then Container → stop nzbfast → Action → Reset.
cu.now.p2: Build (this pulls the new image), then Start.
cu.now.project: If you created it as a Project (Container Manager or Portainer):
cu.pinned: One thing that catches people out: none of this moves a container that was created from a version tag such as :1.0.3. Both Watchtower and a manual re-pull fetch the tag the container was created with, so use :latest if you want updates to arrive.
cu.socket: Worth knowing before you paste it: this needs the Docker socket, and mounting /var/run/docker.sock gives that container root-equivalent control of the machine. If you would rather not, skip it and have your NAS run docker compose pull && docker compose up -d on a schedule instead. On Synology that is Control Panel → Task Scheduler → Create → Scheduled Task → User-defined script, run as root.
cu.stuck: If it does not come back after updating, the container prints why it stopped and the reason is in its own log: Container Manager, then Container, nzbfast, Details, and the Log tab. Over SSH that is docker logs nzbfast. Nothing is lost while it is stopped, and deleting the container or your config folder will not help.

set.cats.rules.hint: give sport, wrestling, podcasts, audiobooks or anything else its own wall category. Each release name runs through these top to bottom, first match wins, ahead of the built-in Movies/TV classifier. Match rules are regexes (plain keywords work too), same as Smart folder rules. "Treat as" decides what happens when a download finishes: movie-like and TV-like get junk cleanup and renaming; "leave as posted" touches nothing, which is the safe choice for books, comics and audio
set.cats.title: Your categories
set.db.cap.hint: how big the index is allowed to get, e.g. 20G. Empty or 0 = no limit. On its own this deletes nothing: the switch below is what acts on it
set.db.evict: Delete releases to stay under it
set.db.evict.hint: off unless you turn it on. With it on, releases are deleted as the index grows past the limit, in the order below; they come back only if a later scan finds them again
set.db.evictnow.hint: run one pass immediately instead of waiting for the index to reach the limit
set.db.kinds.hint: clear a box to protect that kind: those releases are never deleted to save space. Everything ticked = anything can go
set.db.lag: Deleting releases frees space inside the database file, but the file itself only gets smaller once it is compacted, and a compact waits for a moment when nothing is downloading or scanning. So the size above can sit still for a while after a cleanup. The size limit is measured against what is actually stored, not against the space waiting to be reclaimed.
set.db.order.hint: the default ladder spends the least useful entries first, so a full index loses dead fragments long before it loses anything you would search for
set.db.order.ladder: junk and incomplete posts, then oldest, then largest
set.db.shrink.hint: a one-off: delete releases until the index fits the size you type. It does not change the size limit above, and like the limit it leaves the file to be compacted once nothing is downloading or scanning
set.db.stat.free: {free} of that is already free inside the file: it drops to about {live} once a compact rewrites it.
set.db.stat.over: This is over the size limit.
set.db.title: Database
set.disk.cats.hint: the categories offered to Sonarr, Radarr and other clients, and the subfolder each one downloads into. tv, movies, music and books are always available; add any others your apps are set to use - a client whose category is missing here refuses to connect
set.disk.minfree.hint: pause new jobs below this, e.g. 25G; 0 = off
set.disk.move.hint: after unpack and renaming, finished downloads move here - a NAS share, media drive etc. Category subfolders are kept. Empty = leave them in the download folder. If the destination is unreachable the files stay put
set.disk.movecats.hint: override where specific categories land, e.g. tv=/Volumes/NAS/TV, movies=/Volumes/NAS/Movies. The path IS that category's folder. Other categories follow the setting above; empty = no overrides
set.disk.nestdepth.hint: how many archive-in-archive layers to unpack automatically (default 5); applies to the next download. At the limit the deepest archive is left in place, unpacked no further - the download still completes. Raise only for unusually deep nested releases
set.disk.out.hint: completed downloads root (per-category subfolders) · applies to the next download; jobs already queued keep their destination · created automatically if it doesn't exist
set.disk.quota.hint: byte budget per period, e.g. 500G; 0 = off. Force-priority jobs bypass it
set.disk.title: Disk & quota
set.idx.backfill.hint: headers to fetch on a group's first scan
set.idx.can: What it finds: posts that were uploaded under a real filename. The scan reads newsgroup headers, so something posted as Some.Film.2026.1080p.WEB-DL.x264-GROUP.part01.rar is recognised, filed under its title, and shown on the wall with a poster, cast and ratings.
set.idx.cant: What it cannot find: posts with the name taken out. A large and growing share of Usenet is uploaded deliberately obfuscated: the subject is random (p5cbKvaDJ1Y0PW6DvKCIfztzZ), the filenames inside are random too, and it all goes into a catch-all group like alt.binaries.boneless. The real name exists only in an NZB the uploader publishes somewhere else, so it was never posted to Usenet at all and there is nothing on the wire for any scanner to read. This is not a gap we can close later: no competitor recovers those by scanning either.
set.idx.compact.hint: reclaim disk space freed by retention pruning (rewrites the database file). Runs only when no download or scan is active
set.idx.coverage.hint: scan new posts on each of your provider networks, not just one. Posts do not always reach every provider, and providers carry different newsgroups; scanning them all means a release stops looking incomplete when a different provider has the missing parts. The deepest provider still does the history work, the others only follow new posts. Prepaid block accounts are never used for scanning
set.idx.db.browse.title: Browse for the index database file
set.idx.deepen.hint: every scan pass also indexes this many OLDER articles per group, growing history in the background until Max age (or the group's start) is reached; 0 = off
set.idx.dropdb.hint: the database is kept while the indexer is off, so turning it back on picks up where it stopped instead of rescanning. Delete it if you want the disk space back now
set.idx.enabled.hint: off unless you turn it on. It scans the newsgroups you choose, straight from your provider, so you can search and browse Usenet here without a third-party account. Read what it does and does not find below before you decide.
set.idx.gapfill.hint: each scan pass picks this many incomplete releases and asks the other providers for headers around their posting time, filling gaps the scanning provider never received; 0 = off
set.idx.gates.hint: optional JSON filter on what gets indexed: kinds/years/resolutions/languages/title patterns/size, e.g. {"kinds":["tv"],"res":["1080p"],"min_size":"200M"}. Empty = index everything
set.idx.good: Worth turning on if you follow particular newsgroups where people still post under real names, you want to see what your provider actually carries rather than what somebody else says it carries, you want to judge retention and completeness yourself, or you would simply rather not depend on anyone else's service.
set.idx.groups.hint: comma-separated, e.g. alt.binaries.teevee; feeds Browse, the wall and the newznab facade
set.idx.iscdesc.hint: most providers send no descriptions at all, which leaves the group search matching names only. This fetches about 45,000 of them from ISC, a public Usenet directory. It is the only request nzbfast makes to anywhere other than your news provider, so it is off unless you turn it on.
set.idx.leftover: An index from earlier scanning is still on disk: {size}, {n} releases. It is not being read or added to.
set.idx.maxage.hint: only index posts newer than this; 0 = no limit. Keeps the database small
set.idx.noleftover: Nothing is stored: this indexer has never run here.
set.idx.offdoes: With the switch off nothing is scanned, no headers are fetched, no metadata or artwork is looked up, and no availability sampling runs. The poster wall, Browse and the Sonarr/Radarr feed are hidden until you turn it back on. The watchlist stays as long as you have indexer accounts, because it can ask those instead.
set.idx.omdb.hint: optional: richer movie metadata on the wall (exact matches, cast, posters, IMDb ids) and ~4× faster movie enrichment. Free tier is 1,000 lookups/day. Empty = fully keyless
set.idx.omdbget.hint: only needs an email address: we submit the signup for you; OMDb emails you the key with an activation link. Or do it yourself at omdbapi.com/apikey.aspx
set.idx.pausedl.hint: stop indexing entirely while a download is running. Scanning takes NNTP connections from the same account (up to 15 of 20 at the default parallelism) and its database writes compete with the download for CPU and disk. Off = keep indexing during downloads, so new posts stay visible sooner
set.idx.prefq.hint: when one film or episode has been posted several times, releases matching these float to the top of its list and get a “best match” mark. Nothing is ever hidden: release names leave tags out all the time, so this only changes the order. Leave any of them on “no preference” to ignore that one
set.idx.retention.hint: also delete already-stored wall-visible releases once they age past the max-age window, so the index holds ~that window instead of growing forever. Off = only gate new posts. Dead junk fragments (already hidden, still incomplete after a week) are always reaped regardless of this setting
set.idx.scale: For scale, in our own measurements a full index of 14.8 million scanned posts yielded about 31,000 browsable releases. Roughly one in five hundred.
set.idx.scannow.hint: run a scan pass immediately; with a depth, one-off deep backfill: rescan that many recent headers per group even where already scanned (e.g. 500000)
set.idx.title: Indexing
set.idx.wallmeta.hint: clear every cached title/poster and re-download fresh; indexed releases are untouched
set.idx.want.hint: nothing is indexed unless you pick something here. Each choice scans the newsgroups listed under it, and only the ones your provider carries.
set.idx.why: Why a commercial indexer is still recommended: an indexer is told what a release is by whoever uploaded it, so it can name the obfuscated posts that no scanner can. It also carries years of back catalogue, and it is what Sonarr and Radarr expect. Add your accounts under Search indexers just above: searches on the wall can then ask them and grab straight into the queue, with none of this switched on.
set.idx.wipe.hint: delete the whole index database (releases, titles, artwork) and rescan from scratch: the fix for db corruption
set.lib.cats.hint: comma-separated; jobs in these become metadata-only .strm entries, downloaded on first play
set.lib.recheck.hint: how often parked library entries are re-verified (min 60)
set.lib.title: Library
set.look.accent.hint: used for links, buttons and the first chart series
set.look.accent.warn: hard to read on this background
set.look.allpass: Every pair clears the readable minimum.
set.look.border.hint: how visible the line around each card and control is. Strong helps if the edges are hard to make out
set.look.check.hint: measured against the WCAG 2.1 minimum of 4.5:1 for body text
set.look.colours.hint: override the theme's background, card and text colours. The readability check below measures whatever you pick, so you can see immediately if a pair stops being legible
set.look.corners.hint: how rounded cards, buttons and panels are
set.look.density.hint: how much room each card gets. Compact fits every figure in a small window; spacious gives them air
set.look.font.hint: the more readable option picks the clearest faces already installed on this machine (wider letterforms, looser spacing); nothing is downloaded
set.look.motion.hint: charts glide and views fade in. Follows your system's reduce-motion setting unless you choose here
set.look.palette.hint: the series colours on every graph. The colour-blind-safe set stays distinguishable with deuteranopia or protanopia, which a red/green pair does not
set.look.reset.hint: clears everything on this card AND your card layout, in one go: there were two separate resets in two places before
set.look.share.hint: everything on this card, plus your card layout, as a file you can keep or load into another browser
set.look.somefail: Some text on this setting falls below the readable minimum. Pick a different accent, or switch theme.
set.look.theme.hint: Auto follows your system's light or dark setting
set.look.title: Appearance
set.nnab.list.hint: your accounts on NZB indexers (NZBGeek, DrunkenSlug, a Prowlarr or NZBHydra instance, …). Searches on the wall can then ask them too and grab results straight into the queue. API keys never leave this machine. The daily limits mirror your account's allowance: 0 means unlimited.
set.nnab.title: Search indexers
set.notify.body.ph: webhook body, e.g. {"content":"{name} finished"} - empty sends our own JSON. Placeholders: {name} {status} {category} {dir} {bytes} {error} {id}
set.notify.fail.title: also send when a download fails - useful for a chat webhook, noise for a library scan
set.notify.name.title: label for the log line
set.notify.none: no targets: nothing is notified when a download finishes
set.notify.remove.title: Stop notifying this target
set.notify.targets.hint: Kodi, Plex and Jellyfin/Emby get a library rescan; a webhook gets whatever you write, so Discord, ntfy, Gotify and Home Assistant all work. Token = the Plex token, the Jellyfin/Emby API key, or user:password for a Kodi with a password set. Category limits a target to one category; empty = every download. Test sends one now
set.notify.title: Notifications
set.perf.conns.hint: sockets PER SERVER for a download (each server's own account limit also applies); use Connection tuning on the dashboard to find the sweet spot
set.perf.fastverify.hint: claim PAR2 blocks by CRC32 only while downloading: 2-3× faster on slow CPUs; every article's own CRC is still checked and final settle passes always use full MD5. Uncheck for per-block MD5 too
set.perf.mem.hint: pipeline RAM cap, e.g. 8G; 0 = automatic (sized from this machine's RAM)
set.perf.title: Connections & performance
set.remote.body: Point your phone's camera at a code, or type the address - same Wi-Fi works immediately. For access from anywhere, the painless answer is Tailscale (free, no router changes): install it on this machine and your phone, and a "works from anywhere" code appears above automatically. Remote-control apps work too: add nzbfast as a SABnzbd server (this address + your API key) or an NZBGet server (any username, API key as the password). Avoid raw port-forwarding - the dashboard is plain HTTP; if you must, always set an API key.
set.remote.opennote: No API key is set: anyone on your network can control nzbfast at these addresses. Set one in Security below.
set.remote.title: Remote access
set.rename.eg.event: and an event keeps its own words:
set.rename.eg.off: Off: files keep their original names
set.rename.extrawords: Keep the other words in the name
set.rename.extrawords.hint: sport, races and other events are often one title repeated all season, and only a word or two apart: "Round11 Hungary Race" vs "Round11 Hungary Qualifying". Keeping those words is what stops them all becoming the same name. Only applies where the name could not be tidied up otherwise, so ordinary films are untouched
set.rename.identify: Work out what a hidden film is
set.rename.identify.hint: some posts arrive with the name stripped off them, so the video lands as a string of random characters. When that happens, read the film's own running time, picture and sound formats and subtitle languages, then look those up in public film databases. Films only, and only once the download has finished. It renames the file ONLY when two separate databases agree on exactly one film, which needs a TMDB key in your config - without one it never renames, it just writes what it found into History so you can see what the file probably is
set.rename.junk.hint: delete leftover .par2, .nzb, .sfv, .nfo and sample clips from finished movie/TV folders, never the video or its subtitles
set.rename.mediaonly.hint: ⚠ permanently deletes everything except the video(s) and subtitles; every episode of a season pack is kept
set.rename.on.hint: give the folder and main file a clean, informative name: a movie becomes "Example Movie 2024"; TV keeps "Show - S01E02". Obfuscated or unrecognized names are left exactly as posted
set.rename.qbrackets.hint: "… [1080p x265]" instead of "… 1080p x265". Off by default
set.rename.title: Auto-rename & cleanup
set.rename.yearparens.hint: "Example Movie (2024)" instead of "Example Movie 2024". Off by default. Plex, Jellyfin and Radarr match films on the bracketed shape, so turn this on if a media server reads this folder
set.rss.feeds.hint: each feed is polled on its own interval; items passing the rules are queued automatically. Rules (one per line): Require: size>200M · Reject: *480p* · Accept: *1080p*
set.rss.title: RSS auto-grab
set.run.restart.hint: applies the settings above that need a restart. In-progress downloads stop and resume by themselves from where they got to.
set.run.stop.hint: shuts the engine down. Downloads resume where they got to when it starts again.
set.run.title: Run state
set.search.none: Nothing matches that. Try a word from the setting itself, like "quota", "folder" or "key".
set.sec.apikey.confirm: Create a new API key? The old one stops working immediately, so anything already connected (Sonarr, Radarr, NZB360) has to be given the new key.
set.sec.apikey.copied: API key copied to the clipboard.
set.sec.apikey.hint: Sonarr, Radarr, NZB360 and anything else that connects to nzbfast needs this. Show it to copy it across, or create a new one (then paste the new one into those apps). Typing your own here replaces it; leaving it blank keeps the current one
set.sec.apikey.new.ok: New API key created. Paste it into Sonarr, Radarr or anything else that connects to nzbfast.
set.sec.apikey.newcopied: New API key created and copied. Paste it into Sonarr, Radarr or anything else that connects to nzbfast.
set.sec.apikey.none: No key is set: this daemon is open to anyone who can reach it.
set.sec.apikey.shown: API key shown - copy it from the box.
set.sec.nzbkey.hint: add-only key: may submit NZBs but not read or change anything
set.sec.open.title: No API key is set, so every device on your network - and any web page you visit, via CSRF - can control this daemon. Type a key below to require auth.
set.sec.title: Security
set.smart.rules.hint: each added NZB's name runs through these top to bottom: first match wins. Match/but-not are regexes (plain keywords work too); sizes like 200M, 4G; category picks the subfolder of the download root. TV = when the job finishes, file it as [Show]/Season NN/ and rename the video to "Show - S01E02"
set.smart.title: Smart folders
set.snd.blurb: All synthesized right here in the browser: no audio files, nothing stored on the server. Preferences are per-browser.
set.snd.events.hint: uncheck any you don't want · ▶ plays a preview (works even with the master switch off)
set.snd.master.hint: master switch for everything below, including the button-press blip
set.snd.saylen.short: short name: stop before the year/quality
set.snd.saylen.title: how much of a release name to speak
set.snd.speed.hint: ticks: a geiger-style click every N MB downloaded, so a faster line ticks faster (N defaults to about one tick per second at your current speed) · tone: a soft pip every few seconds whose pitch rises and falls with the download rate
set.snd.title: Sounds
set.snd.tts.hint: speak events aloud, naming the file ("Download complete: …") with your browser's built-in voices; nothing leaves this machine · choose which events talk with the 🗣 boxes below
set.snd.voice.hint: the voice list comes from your browser and OS; more can usually be installed in system settings
set.speed.auto.hint: RTT-governed: yields to other household traffic, under the cap
set.speed.autoconn.hint: while idle, measure each provider's connection sweet spot and cap downloads at it: asking a provider for too many sockets can be several times SLOWER than the right number
set.speed.defer.hint: a job stuck on one slow server while others wait is sent to the back of the queue (progress kept; it resumes when the queue is clear)
set.speed.line.hint: your connection's full speed (e.g. 1G, 300M); lets remote apps set percentage speed limits, SABnzbd-style
set.speed.oracleroute: Skip providers the oracle says are gone
set.speed.oracleroute.hint: experimental: when the availability check is confident a provider's backbone has lost a release (takedown), skip it for that download instead of waiting for it to fail. Never skips your last provider. Off by default
set.speed.prefetch.hint: servers the active download can't use (its articles aren't on them) start the next queued job instead of idling; off automatically when a quota is set
set.speed.sched.hint: rules fire in this machine's local time; on (re)start the most recent rule at-or-before now wins
set.speed.title: Speed & scheduling
set.speed.updchecks.hint: show a notice when a new version is published: nzbfast never downloads or installs updates by itself; off = never check at all
set.speed.updurl.hint: release manifest the daemon polls every 6 h; empty disables checking
set.spot.adult: Roughly a third of spots are filed as adult by the people who posted them. Those are left out of Browse unless you tick Include adult there.
set.spot.backfill.hint: how far back to read on the first pass. Later passes carry on from where the last one stopped, so this is paid once
set.spot.cant: What it is not: a replacement for an indexer account. It is a small feed with no back catalogue, so it holds what has been spotted recently rather than everything ever posted. Spots also only cover what somebody chose to announce.
set.spot.enabled.hint: off unless you turn it on. Spotnet is a public feed where people announce what they have posted and sign it with their own key. Each spot carries the real title and the NZB, so it names releases a header scan cannot see. It works with the built-in indexer off.
set.spot.groups.hint: comma-separated. free.pt is the one active Spotnet group; there is rarely a reason to change this
set.spot.title: Spotnet spots
set.spot.what: What it finds: around 170 to 200 new spots a day. Most are Dutch or Belgian, with a steady minority of English scene releases. Every spot is checked against the signature of the person who posted it before it is stored, and one that does not check out is thrown away.
set.spot.where: Spots appear in Browse under their own Spots option, kept separate from your own index so it is always clear which is which. Downloading one fetches the NZB it points at and queues it like any other download.
set.srv.block.hint: prepaid block account: nzbfast tracks lifetime usage and stops using the server when the block is spent. 0 = flatrate. Pair with a tier ≥1 so the block only fills what primaries miss
set.srv.comp.title: of all articles requested from this server over its lifetime, how many it actually had
set.srv.disable.title: Take this server out of the pool without removing it
set.srv.enable.title: Put this server back in the pool
set.srv.fills.title: only queried for articles the primaries could not find: filling those gaps is its whole job, so a lower number here is expected
set.srv.group.hint: servers sharing a name are mirrors of one backbone (optional)
set.srv.import.title: Scan this machine for SABnzbd / NZBGet configs and import their servers
set.srv.level.hint: 0 = primary; a level-N server only fetches articles every lower level missed: fill/backup economics
set.srv.none: no servers configured: add your provider below
set.srv.ret.hint: 0 = unlimited; older articles route to deeper servers
set.srv.test.title: Connect and authenticate to check this server is reachable
set.srv.testall.title: Connect and authenticate to every server at once
set.srv.title: Usenet servers
set.srv.tls.title: Encrypted connection to this server
set.srv.tuned.title: auto-connections measured this provider is fastest at {n} sockets: more were slower. Turn off auto-connections (Connection tuning) to use your set value.
set.srv.warm.hint: reuse this server's connections between downloads instead of opening new ones. Whether it helps depends on your link, so it is off until you measure it: Measure runs a short paired test and tells you what it found. Leave it off for a provider that limits how many addresses you connect from
set.ui.compact.hint: tighten every dashboard card so all the figures fit in a small window: same numbers, less padding. Individual cards can be compacted on their own with the density button in the card header; stored in this browser
set.ui.drop.hint: where the two targets sit when you drag a file onto the page, and which of them gets the room. Stored in this browser
set.ui.herohist.hint: the bar chart under the throughput graph, showing how much time you spend at each speed. Useful for spotting a line that never reaches its peak, noise if you just want the live rate. Stored in this browser
set.ui.histcolor.hint: green for completed, red for failed. Off leaves the names plain - the coloured dot and the row's details still say which is which
set.ui.histrows.hint: how many finished downloads the History card lists before you expand it with the ▤ button; drag the card's bottom edge to make the list scroll instead. Applies to every device viewing this daemon.
set.ui.lang.hint: how this browser shows nzbfast: "System" follows your device language; stored in this browser
set.ui.langd.hint: for embedded webviews and browsers that haven't chosen: "Auto" follows each device's language
set.ui.layout.hint: forget this browser's hidden cards, card order and chart sizes: back to the default layout
set.ui.notify.hint: a system notification when a download completes or fails; the browser will ask permission
set.ui.provsort.hint: seconds between re-ordering the Providers list by live speed (rows slide to their new spot); default 10, 0 keeps the configured order; stored in this browser
set.ui.title: Interface
set.ui.units.hint: how every speed is shown: megabytes (MB/s, the download-manager norm) or megabits (Mb/s, how ISPs quote line speeds). File sizes stay in bytes either way. Applies to every device viewing this daemon.
set.watchdir.cleanup.hint: file extensions deleted from a job's folder once it completes successfully, e.g. par2, sfv, srr, url; empty = off
set.watchdir.dir.hint: .nzb files dropped here are queued (checked every 5 s); empty = off
set.watchdir.faillink.hint: some indexers attach a report link to every NZB they serve. Telling them a post is dead is how they learn to stop offering it, and they usually answer with another copy of the same title. Only works for NZBs fetched by URL (RSS, Add-by-URL, your indexer's "send to" button) - a file you dropped in yourself carries no link. Off by default: it tells a third party what failed for you
set.watchdir.faillink.regrab: report it and queue another copy
set.watchdir.openscript.title: Open the folder containing this script
set.watchdir.script.hint: runs after every job with SABnzbd's args + SAB_* env vars; empty = off
set.watchdir.title: Watch folder & post-processing
setup.s1.hint: the host, username and password are in your provider's welcome email
setup.s2.hint: finished downloads are moved here, one folder per category
setup.s3.hint: optional: pick the kinds of thing you want indexed and they fill a browsable wall, the way a streaming app does. Nothing is indexed until you choose.
setup.title: Setup
shape.title: What this download turned out to be.
shape.why.enc: The files are written straight out as the archive downloads, and the password is applied to the bytes as they arrive - nothing is ever stored locked.
shape.why.mixed: Part of this download was written straight out as it arrived; the rest landed on disk to be unpacked afterwards.
shape.why.ondisk: The archive parts land on disk first and are unpacked once the download finishes.
shape.why.onepass: The files are written straight out as the archive downloads - the archive parts never land on your disk.
shape.why.unlock: Password-protected: the archive downloads locked and is unlocked when the download finishes.
smart.cat.title: category → subfolder of the download root
smart.match.title: matched against the NZB name, case-insensitive
smart.max.title: maximum size, e.g. 20G
smart.min.title: minimum size, e.g. 200M
smart.name.title: rule name (for the log)
smart.none: no rules: downloads go straight to their category folder
smart.not.title: skip this rule when this matches
smart.remove.title: Delete this filing rule
smart.tv.title: file the finished job as [Show]/Season NN/ and rename the video to "Show - S01E02"
snd.ev.mic.title: also announce this event by voice (needs Voice announcements on)
snd.preview.title: Play this sound
stop.confirm: Stop nzbfast? Anything downloading stops and picks up where it left off next time you start it.
stop.done.body: Start it the way you normally do and this page will work again. If it runs under Docker or as a service, it has probably restarted already.
stop.done.title: nzbfast has stopped
toast.compactedNone: Index compacted: already tight, nothing to reclaim.
toast.connsSaved: Saved. {host} now allows up to {n} connections.
toast.deepscan: Deep scan of the last {n} headers started.
toast.evictNone: Nothing to delete: the index is already under the limit.
toast.evictShort: Deleted what it could, but the index is still over the size limit.
toast.evicted.many: {n} releases deleted. The file gets smaller when the compact runs.
toast.evicted.one: {n} release deleted. The file gets smaller when the compact runs.
toast.forced: Moved to the front. Downloads next.
toast.idxfail: Could not change that. The daemon did not accept it.
toast.idxoff: Indexer off. Nothing is scanned, fetched or stored.
toast.idxon: Indexer on. Choose what to index below.
toast.idxpaused: Indexing paused. It stays off until you resume it.
toast.kindsone: Keep at least one kind ticked, or turn the delete switch off.
toast.lnkAdded: Found it. Added to the queue.
toast.lnkBad: That does not look like an nzblnk link.
toast.lnkFast: Too many links at once. Wait a moment and try again.
toast.lnkNone: Nothing found for that link. The post may be too new to have been indexed, or too old to still be on your server.
toast.lnkPartial: Added, but parts are missing so it may not finish.
toast.looknotours: That file isn't an nzbfast appearance file.
toast.metaCleared.many: Cleared metadata for {n} titles - re-downloading in the background.
toast.metaCleared.one: Cleared metadata for {n} title - re-downloading in the background.
toast.needsize: Type a size to shrink to, e.g. 10G.
toast.nochange: Nothing to change. The item may have just finished.
toast.noimport: No SABnzbd or NZBGet configuration found on this machine.
toast.notifyBlocked: Notifications are blocked by the browser.
toast.oldDaemon: This daemon predates the settings API. Rebuild it.
toast.omdbManual: you can request one manually at omdbapi.com/apikey.aspx
toast.omdbReq: Requested! Check your inbox: activate via the link, then paste the key into the OMDb key field.
toast.retried: Requeued: resuming from what already arrived.
toast.short.floor: That is as small as this database gets: what is left is its own structure, not releases.
toast.short.protected: The rest is protected: releases you have watchlisted, queued, downloaded or opened recently are never deleted to save space.
toast.shrinkNone: Already under that size: nothing was deleted.
toast.shrinkShort: Deleted what it could, but the index is still bigger than that.
toast.shrunk.many: {n} releases deleted. The file gives the space back when it is compacted.
toast.shrunk.one: {n} release deleted. The file gives the space back when it is compacted.
toast.srvOff: Server disabled: kept in the list, out of the pool.
toast.srvOn: Server enabled. Back in the pool from the next download.
toast.srvSaved: Server saved: applies from the next download.
toast.updAvail: v{v} is available. See the banner up top.
toast.warmOff: No measurable gain on this link: left it off.
toast.warmOn: Worth keeping open: ticked it for you. Save to apply.
toast.wiped: Index wiped: rescanning starts on the next cycle.
toast.wlAddedCat: Watching {title}. New posts in this category grab automatically.
toast.wlApplied: Watchlist applied. Checking the index now.
toast.zipfail: Could not read {name} as a zip.

wall.badge.par2.title: Repair data posted alongside: damaged parts can be rebuilt
wall.dens.l.title: Large posters
wall.dens.m.title: Medium posters
wall.dens.s.title: Small posters, more on screen
wall.dens.title: Poster density
wall.dir.title: Reverse the order - oldest, smallest or lowest first
wall.dupe.body.have: {name} is already in your completed downloads.
wall.dupe.title.queued: This is already in your queue
wall.empty.none: Nothing indexed yet. Choose which newsgroups to index and the wall fills itself.

wall.exp.title: Show this title's releases
wall.ext.grabs: How often this indexer’s users grabbed it
wall.ext.typeq: Type a search to ask your indexers - browsing them would spend your daily API allowance.

wall.getnzb.title: Download the .nzb file
wall.group.title: Cluster the wall by category (TV / Movies / Apps) - the sort applies within each section
wall.grpby.title: One row per title, its releases nested underneath
wall.hid.sub: Hide a few similar titles and the wall learns: it will suggest a filter you can accept with one click.

wall.hide.title: Hide this title from the wall; undo any time under “Hidden”
wall.home.title: Downloads and status
wall.hover.title: Rest the pointer on a row for a poster and synopsis popup - everything from your own index

wall.person.allhave: Nothing else found - you already have everything these sources list.

wall.spot.adult.title: Spots are filed by the person who posted them. Roughly a third of them are filed as adult.

wall.spot.src: Posted by {who}, who signed this spot

wall.sug.lang: Hide all {v}-tagged releases from now on?
wall.sug.other: Hide all {v} entries from now on?
wall.sug.word: Hide everything containing “{v}” from now on?
wall.trailer.title: Search YouTube for a trailer in a new tab - nothing is fetched or stored here
wall.unm.title: Show the hidden unmatched entries
wall.vd.gone: Probably taken down: the availability check keeps missing its parts
wall.view.releases.title: Every release in a sortable table
wall.view.title: Choose how titles are laid out
wall.view.wall.title: Browse titles as a poster wall
wall.viewmenu.title: Layout, sorting and filters

wall.watch.movie: auto-grab this film when it appears (or a better version than what's here)
wall.watch.tv: auto-grab new episodes as they appear, upgrading quality automatically

watch.cat.title: category folder for grabs
watch.eps.title: episodes within those series: 1-13 · 1,3,5-7 · blank = all
watch.ext: Also search my indexer accounts for wanted items
watch.ext.title: Each watched item asks your indexer accounts about twice a day, and only for things it has not found here. Your daily limits still apply.
watch.extoff: the built-in indexer is off, so there is no local index to match against. Tick “Also search my indexer accounts” below and this watchlist works off your indexer accounts instead.
watch.extonly: asks your indexer accounts about wanted items a couple of times a day · min = floor · upgrade-to = ceiling
watch.idxoff: indexing is off, so the watchlist has nothing to match against.
watch.idxoff2: or pick newsgroups in ⚙ settings → Indexing.
watch.min.title: minimum quality worth grabbing
watch.none: nothing watched yet: add a show or film below (even one that hasn’t aired); it’s grabbed automatically the moment a matching post lands in a scanned group.
watch.remove.title: Remove this from the watchlist
watch.replace.title: after an upgrade finishes downloading, delete the older version
watch.seasons.title: series/seasons to grab: 3 · 1-4 · 2,4 · blank = all
watch.st.none: nothing grabbed yet: watching for a matching post
watch.status: matches everything indexed from {groups} (the watched newsgroups; edit them in ⚙ settings → Indexing) · min = floor · upgrade-to = ceiling
watch.target.title: stop upgrading once a grab reaches this
watch.title: Watchlist
watch.upgrade.title: keep grabbing better versions until the target quality is reached
